newsitem.title: UK: Credit Lyonnais EC aid conditions - paper.
newsitem.headline: Credit Lyonnais EC aid conditions - paper.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to tell France's state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais that it must sell all remaining European banking operations outside its national base in return for approval of a rescue package of up to 3.2 billion stg said the Financial Times on Wednesday.
The FT said the troubled bank could face further demands to cut its domestic branch network, seen by the Commission as too expensive, and sell off part of its wholesale banking interests.

But the report said people close to the negotiations believed Credit Lyonnais had limited room for manouvre in reducing its activities if it is to meet objectives set for it in a pre-privatisation plan which is being finalised.
Sales of part of the group's assets would also reduce the privatisation price and possibly trigger further capital losses which would require more state aid.

Last week French finance minister Jean Arthuis said he did not expect details of the rescue proposals until the end of March. The plans will decide on state aid ahead of privatisation earmarked for the end of next year or 1999
